$comment: Generated by scripts/generate-jstack-trees.py from features/, skills/, playbooks/, templates/ and the pstack map of THIRD_PARTY.md: do not edit. A skill or principle is a name a brief's Skills: line may use, and so is a playbook marked nameable. hidden: a skill a model may not load by itself, which its feature.json lists. source: `pstack` is pstack's item of the same name, brought over one to one; `adapted` is built from pstack's item with other material, or from a pstack item of another name, which `pstack_name` gives; `jstack` is jstack's own, with no pstack skill or principle behind it, though it may borrow a passage from a pstack reference file. THIRD_PARTY.md says what each took and what changed. hooks: each hook script, the harnesses that run it, which the install links into each harness's layout, and each settings entry the install writes for it. statusLine: the script the install sets as Claude Code's status line. gitHooks: each hook the install links into a main checkout. projectSkills: each skill of this repo's own, which the install links into a checkout's .claude/skills and .cursor/skills by its name.

items.name: principle-attack-the-premise
items.description: Apply when two or more fixes that share one premise have failed the same gate. Write the premise down and test it directly before you write another fix that assumes it.

items.name: principle-boundary-discipline
items.description: Apply when wiring validation, error handling, or framework adapters. Concentrate guards at system boundaries (CLI, config, network, external APIs); trust internal types and keep business logic in pure functions.

items.name: principle-build-the-lever
items.description: Apply when a need repeats: the second time you meet the same edit, migration, analysis, or check, not the first. Build the tool that does it or proves it (codemod, script, generator, or a skill your subagents follow) instead of working by hand again. The tool is the artifact a reviewer can rerun.

items.name: principle-depth-over-breadth
items.description: Apply when scoping research, perf, analysis or outcome work: before a brief goes out, and before you plan how to do one. Go one level under the task, to the data, the instruments and the judge a field-leading expert would use, instead of adding a second task beside it.

items.name: principle-encode-lessons-in-structure
items.description: Apply when you catch yourself writing the same instruction a second time, or notice a recurring correction. Encode the rule as a lint, metadata flag, runtime check, or script instead of more text.

items.name: principle-exhaust-the-design-space
items.description: Apply when facing a novel UI interaction or architectural decision with no precedent in the codebase. Build 2-3 competing prototypes and compare side by side before committing.

items.name: principle-experience-first
items.description: Apply when product, UX, or feature-scope tradeoffs come up. Choose user delight over implementation convenience; ship fewer polished features over more rough ones.

items.name: principle-explain-the-number
items.description: Apply before you measure, and before you trust, report, or act on a number you measured: a speedup, a regression, a throughput, a latency, or an eval result. Find what limits it, and rule out that it measured something other than the work you think.

items.name: principle-fix-root-causes
items.description: Apply when debugging. Trace each symptom back to the first place the system went wrong and fix it there. A guard is a fix only when the state it handles is legitimate.

items.name: principle-foundational-thinking
items.description: Apply before writing logic: choosing core types and data structures, sequencing scaffold-vs-feature work, asking what concurrent actors share. Get the data structures right so downstream code becomes obvious.

items.name: principle-guard-the-context-window
items.description: Apply when context is filling up: large outputs, long files, repeated reads, fan-out planning. Route bulk to subagents; keep summaries in the main thread, not raw payloads.

items.name: principle-laziness-protocol
items.description: Apply when refactoring, evaluating diff size, or tempted to add abstractions, layers, or signal threading. Bias toward deletion and the smallest change that solves the problem.

items.name: principle-make-operations-idempotent
items.description: Apply when designing commands, lifecycle steps, or processing loops that run amid crashes, restarts, and retries. Converge to the same end state regardless of partial prior runs.

items.name: principle-migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis
items.description: Apply when introducing a new internal API while old callers still exist. Migrate callers and delete the old API in the same wave instead of preserving compatibility layers.

items.name: principle-minimize-reader-load
items.description: Apply when reviewing or shaping code that's hard to trace. Count layers between question and answer, and hidden state in the reader's head; collapse one-caller wrappers and shrink mutable scope.

items.name: principle-model-the-domain
items.description: Apply when writing stateful logic, or when code branches a lot or repeats a shape assumption across files.

items.name: principle-never-block-on-the-human
items.description: Apply when tempted to ask 'should I do X?' on reversible work.

items.name: principle-outcome-oriented-execution
items.description: Apply during planned rewrites and migrations with explicit phase boundaries. Converge on the target architecture; don't preserve smooth intermediate states with throwaway compatibility code.

items.name: principle-prove-it-works
items.description: Apply after completing a task, before declaring done. Verify against the real artifact (run the feature, read the actual value, inspect the diff), not a proxy, self-report, or 'it compiles.'

items.name: principle-redesign-from-first-principles
items.description: Apply when integrating a new requirement into an existing design.

items.name: principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state
items.description: Apply when concurrent actors might write to the same file, branch, key, or state object. Eliminate the sharing first; serialize structurally only when one shared writer is a real invariant.

items.name: principle-sequence-verifiable-units
items.description: Apply to multi-step work (sweeps, migrations, runs of similar edits) and to how you order commits and pull requests. Break work into small units that each end in a verifiable state, check each before the next, and order delivery so the sequence proves itself to a reviewer.

items.name: principle-subtract-before-you-add
items.description: Apply when sequencing an addition, refactor, or rewrite. Remove dead code, redundant validators, and stub references first, then build on the simpler base.

items.name: principle-test-behavior-not-implementation
items.description: Apply when you write, change, or keep a test. Assert what the code's users can observe, so that the test fails when that behavior breaks and keeps passing when only the internals change.

items.name: principle-type-system-discipline
items.description: Apply when designing types, reviewing a function signature, or writing code in any statically-typed language. Make illegal states unrepresentable, brand semantic primitives, parse external data at boundaries, exhaust variants, derive from authoritative schemas.

items.name: architect
items.description: Sketch the types, signatures and module layout before writing code for non-trivial work. Use when asked to architect or design something, or when coding first would lock in the wrong shape.

items.name: arena
items.description: Make one artifact twice, apart, as two runner crews, have a judge crew score both, and a graft crew pick a base and graft the other's best into it. Typed in a home. Use for /arena, 'arena this', or 'throw it in the arena'.

items.name: automate-me
items.description: Use for /automate-me, "automate me", "create/update/refresh my -mode skill", "turn/capture my preferences or working style into a skill", or wanting agents to follow how the user works. Drafts or revises a personal -mode skill by the authoring-a-skill playbook and unslop, optionally pulling fresh evidence from recent transcripts.

items.name: benchmark-checklist
items.description: Vet a measured number before it is reported or acted on: its limiter, tuning, errors, repeatability and whether the work ran. Use when a speedup, regression, latency or eval result is about to be trusted.

items.name: blast-radius
items.description: Find what a change could break beyond its diff, and prove the one fact it is safe because of by running real code. Use for 'blast radius of X', 'what could this break', or a small diff you do not trust.

items.name: bro
items.description: Restate the last message in plain words with no jargon. Use when the user says they did not follow, or asks for it in plain English.

items.name: correct
items.description: Find the mistakes agents keep repeating in a repo and make each one impossible - structure first, then types, then a test, and a written rule last - and prove each check fails on a real past mistake. Runs only when the user types /correct or $correct, or a brief names it.

items.name: create-formal-verification-skill
items.description: Generate a project-local skill that formally verifies the code where a bug costs most and tests reach least. Use for 'model-check this race', 'prove this invariant', or concurrency, retries, state machines and parsers that need more than tests.

items.name: create-verification-skill
items.description: Generate a project-local verify-[app] skill that drives the repo's app the way a user does. Use for 'make a verify skill for this repo', or when a repo has no scripted way to prove UI, CLI or service behavior.

items.name: crew
items.description: Make this thread a crewmate - do the one task a home wrote a brief for, in this thread's own worktree, write the result back to the brief, and stay on the pull request it opened. Use when the user or a home starts a thread with /crew <slug> or $crew <slug>.

items.name: expert
items.description: Make this thread an expert - the always-on subject matter expert whose folder is named, which researches and answers asks about its one subject from its sources and its notes, and never writes code. Use when the user or another thread starts a thread with /expert <name> or $expert <name>.

items.name: figure-it-out
items.description: Frame a task no playbook fits (a large migration, an ambitious multi-part change, work reviewed after stepping away) and, in a home, plan it as entries. Use for 'figure it out'.

items.name: grilling
items.description: Question the user about a plan, decision or idea, one round at a time through the question form, until nothing is left assumed. Use for 'grill me', 'walk me through these one by one', 'ask me the questions', or open choices left to decide.

items.name: handoff
items.description: Archive this home - stop what runs, keep a note of ten lines at most in its log, hand what it has out to the root home, close its scope, switch off its scheduled tasks, and rename and settle this thread. It starts no next home. Use when the user invokes /handoff or $handoff, archives a home from the jstack tree, or says to archive or close this home.

items.name: home
items.description: Make this thread the home for the repo it runs in - read where things stand, plan work with the user, and hand each task to a crewmate thread. A home runs until it is archived with /handoff. Use when the user invokes /home or $home, opens a new thread to continue work in a repo, or asks to pick up where the last thread left off.

items.name: how
items.description: Explain how a subsystem works, its runtime flow and where code belongs, before changing it. Use for 'how does X work', a walkthrough, or 'where should this live'. Use why for motivation.

items.name: in-your-own-words
items.description: Restate what the user is after, and the problem behind it, before any work starts. Use when an ask is long or ambiguous, or the user asks what you think they want.

items.name: interrogate
items.description: Adversarially review a change with two reviewers that do not see each other, then filter what they found. Use for 'challenge this', 'stress test this code', 'find blind spots' or 'tear this apart'.

items.name: ketchup
items.description: Catch the user up on what changed in this chat since their last message, with every item waiting on them. Use for 'catch me up on this thread' or 'what did I miss'. For past sessions, use recall.

items.name: maintain-formal-verification-skill
items.description: Bring a project's formal verification back in line after the code changed: update the model, rerun, and say whether each failure is drift or a bug. Use for 'is the model still true to the code', or after merges touched verified code.

items.name: maintain-verification-skill
items.description: Keep a repo's verify skill, `.claude/skills/verify-<app>/` or a `verify-<app>` project skill, and its feature map honest as the app changes: typed in the repo's home, it sends one scout per feature file to read the feature from source, then writes one crewmate brief for the live pass over every feature and at most one pull request of proven corrections. Use for /maintain-verification-skill or "audit the verify skill".

items.name: make-bot-ui
items.description: Build a page whose buttons wake this T3 Code thread through a schedule_task webhook, served on the tailnet by a local server that keeps the webhook's URL and key off the browser. Use for /make-bot-ui, 'make a bot UI', 'buttons that wake this thread'.

items.name: new-home
items.description: Set up a repo's first home - its state directory, its T3 Code project, its table in jbus's config, what it lacks for jbus to merge in it, and its home thread. It finishes a home that was started by hand, and does only what is missing. Use for /new-home <repo>.

items.name: no-comments
items.description: Hunt down every code comment with no reason to stay, delete it, and fix the code it was excusing. Use for 'remove useless comments' or a comment cleanup over a scope.

items.name: nohome
items.description: Opt out of the automatic home - make this thread an ordinary thread, or switch the automatic home off or back on for the whole repo, or switch the repo's automatic merge off or back on. Use when the user invokes /nohome or $nohome, or says this thread should not be a home, should just do the work itself, or should stop planning and handing out.

items.name: poteto-help
items.description: Answer a help question about jstack: setup, which role takes a piece of work, and which playbook and skills fit a brief. Use for 'how do I do X in jstack', 'which playbook fits', or 'what do I type'.

items.name: pr-review
items.description: Have a finished pull request reviewed in a fresh thread - one review thread per pull request reads its diff itself, judges what it found, and proves the one safety fact by running code (pstack's review, with no reviewer subagents and no fixes), and records the findings in the brief, where jbus reads them and tells the thread that did the work when it owes a line. Use when the user invokes /pr-review or $pr-review in a home or in a crewmate's thread, or asks to review the pull requests that have finished.

items.name: recall
items.description: Rebuild where the user left off across past sessions, from chat history and the home's record. Use for 'where did I leave off', 'what was I working on', 'recall my work on X'. For this chat alone, use ketchup.

items.name: reflect
items.description: Read one thread's transcript with three review subagents and a synthesiser, and end in proposed edits and proposed plan entries for the home to put to the user. It starts four subagents and edits nothing. Runs only when the user types /reflect or $reflect, or a brief names it.

items.name: retro
items.description: Audit what happened over a past window from the raw records: build a dataset you can rerun, freeze a codebook before reading any outcome, sharpen the prompt, and send scouts, with a second labeller, a red team, and rates that show their row mix. Use for /retro, 'audit what happened over <window>', 'take a census of', 'what went wrong last week'.

items.name: scout
items.description: Make this thread a scout - research the one question a home wrote a request for, with read-only tool calls over the code and the docs, write the report (and the crewmate's brief or a visual when asked), and tell the home. Use when the user or a home starts a thread with /scout <slug> or $scout <slug>.

items.name: setup-pstack
items.description: Set this machine up for jstack, or check it again - run the checkout's own `install.sh --setup`, or a release's `jinstall --setup`, which walks every need once, writes the configs that are not there and links the units, then the doctor, and report what was done, what was already there and the one command for each thing only the user can do. Use for /setup-pstack.

items.name: sharpen
items.description: Rewrite a task's prompt to ask for the deeper version, not a bigger one, without doing the task. Use for 'sharpen this', 'make this prompt better', or a long hand-typed brief or audit ask before it goes out.

items.name: show-me-your-work
items.description: Keep a decision log, one TSV row per decision, for long or unattended work. Use when the user will step away and review later, or asks to see your work or your decisions.

items.name: statechart
items.description: Draw what an app's user sees as a Mermaid statechart from a TLA+ model, each bug TLC finds a numbered path. Use for 'show the PM the bug', or to turn an agreed chart into a TLA+ skeleton.

items.name: swarm
items.description: Fan a task out to up to ten scout and crew threads a step, drain them, and build one table from their Reports and Results. Typed in a home. Use for /swarm, 'swarm this', or parallel coverage, races, gauntlets and exploration.

items.name: tdd
items.description: Fix a bug test-first, with a focused regression test that fails before the fix and passes after. Use for a bug with a clear, cheap test path; skip it when the test would be slow or integration-heavy.

items.name: teach
items.description: Explain a body of work plainly until the user understands it, using how and why. Use for 'teach me this', 'help me really understand X', or explaining a change or subsystem.

items.name: technical-writing
items.description: Write or review docs, READMEs, RFCs, PR descriptions and commit messages to a layered standard: Diataxis structure, Google developer style, STE rules and Global English.

items.name: typescript-best-practices
items.description: TypeScript best practices. Use before reading or editing .ts or .tsx files.

items.name: unslop
items.description: Cut AI tells from writing. Use when the user says text reads like AI, asks to unslop it, or before prose ships to people.

items.name: unstick
items.description: Find why rows of the jbus queue have not moved, from jbus's own records: each stalled row's cause and age, the reversible step that moves it taken at once, and the rest parked as gates. Use for /unstick, 'why are we stalled', 'why is nothing moving', 'why do these crewmates look stalled'.

items.name: why
items.description: Find why code is the way it is, from its history and every evidence source this session can query, with citations. Use for 'why does X work this way', 'why did we pick Y', regressions and postmortems. Use how for runtime behavior.
